title: store
description: What a feature keeps: the connection its records live behind, and the collections kept there -- each a shape, under a name, keyed by one of its fields. A store declares; it runs nothing. Data graphs read and write its collections through the operations of @storage/store.port.json, naming the store and the collection and nothing else: the collection is where the record type is written down. Lives in a feature's data/ directory, since how records are kept is the data layer's job.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/store.schema.json.

description.description: What this store keeps, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

connection.description: The connection the records live behind, by path. Its kind must be one a storage engine plugin grants -- one whose connection kind document says "storage": true.

reads.description: The reads this store's collections are scoped by: local name -> the resolver that declares it, as @feature/edge/file.resolvers.json#name, the way a data graph or a binding binds one. Every entry is read by some collection's `scoped` (P005), and the compiler carries the read to every storage operation over that collection, so no document writes a scope.

collections.description: name -> what is kept under it. The name is how a call site names the collection, and it is the name the engine keeps the records under, so two stores over one connection that declare the same name mean the same collection. A collection is one of two shapes: it keeps records (`of` and `key`), or it is a `view` of one that does, seeing every row `behind` a policy.

of.description: The record type: the path of a core shape, or of a shape a plugin grants. This is the one place the type is written; a call site names the store and the collection instead of repeating it.

key.description: The field of `of` that identifies a record: required, and of whatever type the shape gives it -- that is the type get, patch and remove take and newKey answers.

unique.description: The combinations no two records may repeat: each inner list is one constraint over those fields together, so [["url", "method"]] is one constraint on the pair and [["url"], ["method"]] is two constraints, one on each. The key is unique already and is never listed here.

refs.description: field -> the collection whose key that field holds. A record whose reference names nothing is refused, and so is removing a record another still references. The reference stays within this store, and the field's type is the referenced collection's key's type.

collection.description: The collection of this store whose key this field holds.

onRemove.description: What removing a referenced record does. refuse is the only value: a removal that would orphan a record is refused, and nothing is ever deleted on a tree's behalf.

description.description: What this reference means, for a reader of a graph that writes it.

defaults.description: field -> the literal existing records receive when ensure adds that field's column to a table that already holds rows. It is about existing rows, never about what a graph writes: a put still gives the whole record, and whether a field may be absent is the shape's required: false, said once. A key is never defaulted.

renamed.description: Fields of the shape that changed name, each keyed by its name now and holding its name before, so `wilanis migrate` renames the column instead of dropping one and adding another. Remove the entry once every database has applied it; the planner says when. A name may appear once as a value.

was.description: The collection's name before this one on the same connection, so `wilanis migrate` renames the table instead of dropping it and creating another. Remove it once every database has applied it.

scoped.description: column -> the read that fills it. Each key names a column the store keeps beside the record, which the shape does not declare. Each value is exactly {{<name>}} for a name the store binds under `reads`: one whole read, no literal, no interpolation, no field of it. The compiler puts the read on every operation over this collection as `scope`; no document writes `scope`. The engine writes the columns on put and puts them on every statement, and `unique` constraints hold within the scope.

view.description: The scoped collection of this store whose rows this one sees, across every scope.

behind.description: The policy every trigger that reaches an operation over this view must attach, by path. A view is the one way across a scope, and this says what guards it.

description.description: What this collection holds, for a reader of a graph that reads or writes it.

if.description: `view` is what tells the two shapes apart, so an author is answered about the one they wrote.

then.description: A view of a scoped collection of this store: the `behind` it is seen through, and nothing a kept collection declares -- it has the viewed collection's shape, key and constraints.

else.description: A collection that keeps records: `of` and `key`, and no `behind`, which is a view's.
